title: I Let the Tattoo Aftercare Photo Policy Hit the Artist Who Skipped It

parts.text: I sat for a touch-up at 3:12 p.m. and the artist started without the aftercare photo the studio required. The policy on the iPad he designed said: BEFORE PHOTO. AFTERCARE SHEET SIGNED. NO INK WITHOUT BOTH. I was twenty-seven, returning client, holding an unsigned sheet. Artist Finn said, "I remember your skin." I pointed at the iPad. He gloved up. "Artists are the chart." I photographed the blank photo slot, the iPad, and the unsigned sheet. Then I asked the shop manager to pause the machine. At 3:16 the manager asked why Finn's name was on a skipped-chart ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The manager can see a blank before-photo slot against the iPad policy Finn designed.

social.video_title: He skipped the aftercare photo he designed — Part 1/2
social.description: Touch-up, an unsigned sheet, and an iPad policy. I paused the machine. Would you have sat anyway?

parts.text: Finn called it a shortcut until insurance asked for the chart. I printed the ticket, the iPad, and the photo of the blank. We did the before photo. Finn inked after the sheet and told the shop the iPad was always about optics. Optics is a word artists use when a pause exists. Chart policy now has a second line: MEMORY IS NOT A BEFORE PHOTO. I heal on paper. Finn taps the slot. The machine finally waits.

social.video_title: Memory is not a before photo — Part 2/2
social.description: Skipped-chart ticket, a real before photo, and a second line on the iPad. Was skin ever a shortcut?
